description: The allowlist the automation engine reads before it goes near a field. It ships empty and is fail-closed: a field that is not listed here can neither be tested by a rule, nor watched for changes, nor written to by one. A System Manager curates the list; ops then author rules inside it.

fields.label: DocType Name
fields.description: The record the field lives on — CRM Lead, CRM Task, and so on. A field is allowlisted per doctype, so status on a task and status on a lead are two separate rows and are permitted separately.

fields.label: Fieldname
fields.description: The field's internal name rather than the label a rep sees — status, custom_substage, outcome. It is the name a rule refers to, so a typo here does not error; the rule simply never matches anything.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Unticked, the row is ignored altogether and the field goes back to being disallowed — the allowlist is fail-closed, so withdrawing a field is a matter of unticking it rather than deleting the row and losing its grain scope.

fields.label: What Rules May Do With It
fields.description: Nothing is permitted until it is ticked here. The three permissions are independent and are granted one at a time: a field can be safe to read and still be dangerous to write.

fields.label: Can Read
fields.description: A rule may test this field in its criteria — 'status is Done', 'city is Pune'. Reading lets a rule look at the field and nothing more: a change to it starts nothing, and no rule can write to it.

fields.label: Can Watch
fields.description: A change to this field may start a rule, and a rule may test the change itself — 'status moved from Open to Done'. This is what turns the field into a trigger rather than a condition. Watching implies reading, so a watched field can always be tested as well.

fields.label: Can Set
fields.description: A rule's Set Field action may write this field. It is the only tick that lets an automation change patient data, so it is the one to be sparing with — once granted, any rule inside the grain below can overwrite the field on every record it covers.

fields.label: Where A Set Writes
fields.description: By default a Set writes the field on the record itself. Fill these in only when it should write into a child table instead.

fields.label: Child Table Field
fields.description: The table on the parent record to write into — left blank, the Set writes the parent's own field. Named, the Set writes into a row of that table, and Fieldname above is read as a column inside it.

fields.label: Is Row Key
fields.description: The column a child-row Set matches on to decide whether it is updating a row that already exists or adding a new one. With no row key, every run of the rule adds another row.

fields.label: Which Grains May Set It
fields.description: The write is confined to the grain named here. Each level left blank is a wildcard, and a row left wholly blank lets any grain's rule write the field. Reading and watching are never scoped this way — the grain governs writes alone.

fields.label: Vertical
fields.description: The product line a rule must belong to before it may write this field. Blank is a wildcard.

fields.label: Group
fields.description: Narrows the write further, to one group inside that vertical. Blank is a wildcard.

fields.label: Program
fields.description: The narrowest scope of the three: only a rule under this program may write the field. Blank is a wildcard.

name: CRM Automation Field
